title: eriophorum gracile subsp. hoefftii
intro: Eriophorum gracile subsp. hoefftii, commonly known as Hoefft's cotton-grass, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Cyperaceae. This plant is traditionally used in herbal medicine for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of respiratory issues, digestive problems, and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Hoefft's cotton-grass are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and promote wound healing, making it a valuable resource in natural medicine. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other secondary metabolites that contribute to its medicinal properties.
